topics.topic: Environment bindings, defaults, and startup rules for deployment-configurable runtime settings
questions: For each listed knob without an `_env_name`, can deployment override it, through which environment variable, what values are valid, and what happens when the value is missing or invalid?
What are the configuration keys, environment names, requiredness, defaults, and startup refusal rules for the A25 transport settings that A30 is said to provide?
For every deployment-variable knob, what is its exact environment-variable name, type, requiredness, normalization, and default or per-environment default?
For each newly deployment-variable knob, what environment variable supplies it, and does absence select the stated default or stop startup?

quotes:
Values are knobs; the *existence* of a timeout/TTL/rate limit is an
invariant, its value is config.

- `config.runtime_environment_variables`: the closed table of environment
  variables, their types, requiredness, normalization and per-environment
  defaults, read into `RuntimeSettings` (R0-10; Factory `a6916180314d`,
  `51d19fdf`).
judgement.why: The reopening change did not touch A30's missing environment bindings or its referenced but unstated configuration table and did not make that omission newly consequential.

topics.topic: Minimum credential entropy and security closure for deployment-controlled configuration
questions: What minimum and maximum credential entropy values are permitted, and must startup reject a deployment override that is below the security requirement?
How can the security review remain resolved if a deployment may select an arbitrarily small credential entropy value, and what minimum or fixed constraint closes that category?
Is the configuration-input security category actually closed, and if so, what complete validation table closes it?

quotes:
Values are knobs; the *existence* of a timeout/TTL/rate limit is an
invariant, its value is config.

- one or more independently revocable credentials, generated with sufficient
  entropy, shown only at creation or rotation, stored only in verification
  form, rotatable with an overlap period, never carried by staff or viewer
  contours, never logged;
judgement.why: The reopening change touched neither the deployment-variable entropy setting nor the existing sufficient-entropy requirement and did not create their missing validation relationship.

provenance.quote: - one or more independently revocable credentials, generated with sufficient entropy, shown only at creation or rotation

topics.topic: Accepted values and startup validation for numeric runtime settings
questions: What ranges are accepted for each numeric knob, and do zero or negative values mean disabled, immediate expiry, or invalid startup configuration?
Which deployment values are valid for each numeric knob, including whether zero, negative, fractional, extremely large, or syntactically malformed values stop startup?

quotes:
Values are knobs; the *existence* of a timeout/TTL/rate limit is an
invariant, its value is config.

- The existence of every timeout, TTL, rate limit and bound is invariant; its
  value is configuration.
judgement.why: The accepted ranges and parsing rules for numeric runtime settings were already absent from unchanged A30 text before this reopening.

topics.topic: Configuration and relationship of trusted hosts, CORS origins, and the canonical public origin
questions: What exact value is the canonical public origin, where does it come from, and may it differ from or be one member of the CORS allowlist?
How are trusted hosts, allowed CORS origins, and the one canonical public origin configured and validated, and must the canonical origin be a member of the CORS allowlist?

quotes:
The service answers only on its trusted hosts (at least one, no wildcard at any
position); CORS is off when its allowlist is empty, and an allowed origin is
never a wildcard.

The
viewer browser session is the host-only cookie of R0-09; a viewer sign-out
must come from the canonical public origin (viewer entry is not
origin-checked), compared by scheme, host
and effective port, with no pattern matching.

The service is
configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts,
and answers only on the trusted hosts it is
configured with; wildcard hosts and origins are refused.
judgement.divergence: With two allowed origins, one implementation designates the origin that sends sign-out as canonical and revokes the session, while another designates the other origin as canonical and refuses sign-out; the viewer observes whether the session ends.
judgement.why: The texts require trusted hosts, a CORS allowlist and one canonical public origin but do not define the canonical value or its relationship to the allowlist.

witness.initial: A deployment has two non-wildcard allowed origins and a viewer has an active cookie session.
events: The deployment operator configures the service's trusted host and allowed origins.
The viewer sends sign-out from one of the allowed origins.
outcomes: That allowed origin is selected as the canonical public origin, so sign-out succeeds and the session is revoked.
The other allowed origin is selected as the canonical public origin, so sign-out is refused and the session remains active.
basis:
The service answers only on its trusted hosts (at least one, no wildcard at any
position); CORS is off when its allowlist is empty, and an allowed origin is
never a wildcard.

The
viewer browser session is the host-only cookie of R0-09; a viewer sign-out
must come from the canonical public origin (viewer entry is not
origin-checked), compared by scheme, host
and effective port, with no pattern matching.
Viewers can restore and end their session explicitly.

provenance.quote: The service is configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts, and answers only on the trus
Viewers can restore and end their session explicitly.

topics.topic: Request-body and binary-response size ceilings and refusal behavior
questions: What is the maximum request-body size, which requests it covers, how streamed or chunked bodies are counted, and what exact refusal occurs when the declared or actual size exceeds it?
What is the request-body ceiling, and is the binary response ceiling identical to `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` or a separate setting?

quotes: Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime settings before expensive work;

Content exceeding `binary_max_read_bytes` is rejected before response
emission.
judgement.why: The reopening change did not touch the request-body or binary size-bound passages and did not make their missing values or counting rules newly relevant.

topics.topic: Viewer-entry rate-limit parameters, storage policy, and over-limit response
questions: What exact viewer-entry limit, time window, memory bound, eviction algorithm, and concealed over-limit response apply, and which of them are configurable?
What are the viewer-entry attempt limit, time window, retained-client bound, and observable over-limit response?

quotes:
An entry attempt over the limit is refused before any
code verification and creates no session; the limiter's algorithm, its
bound and its answer are those of the accepted transport guard
(`rules.http_transport_policy.limits.viewer_entry`), with the values of
A30, carried to States 6–7.
judgement.why: The reopening change did not touch the viewer-entry limiter reference or A30's omission of its parameters and did not make that omission newly consequential.

topics.topic: Whether EMAIL_GATEWAY_URL is required while email functionality is inert
questions: While all email operations are inert, must startup require and validate `EMAIL_GATEWAY_URL`, or may it be absent until Q19 is implemented?
Must the running service refuse startup when `EMAIL_GATEWAY_URL` is absent even though all email operations are inert?

quotes:
Delivery-only boundary for staff-account mail: email-verification,
email-change, and password-reset challenges plus security notifications,
all deferred in the accepted service (R0-23), so the gateway is called by no
operation of the running portal.
judgement.why: The reopening change touched neither the inert email boundary nor A30's failure to state whether EMAIL_GATEWAY_URL is required at startup.

topics.topic: Precedence and rate-limiter side effects when multiple transport checks fail
questions: In a request that violates more than one transport condition, which failure wins, and may an earlier failure consume viewer-entry rate-limit capacity?

quotes:
For every request, in order: a request id with no identity in it; 400 for an
untrusted host; CORS preflight 204 for a listed origin and 403 for another;
403 for a viewer logout from another origin than the public one; 413 for a
body over `max_request_body_bytes`; 429 for viewer entries over the
monotonic-clock rate limit, before any credential is parsed; then the route,
called once.
The in-memory viewer-entry attempt buckets only.
judgement.why: State 5 fixes the transport-check order, so an oversized viewer-entry request is refused before the rate limiter and cannot update its attempt buckets.
